gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-serif-khojki: Noto Serif Khojki is a quiet text serif with short ascenders. Gugi's bent-straw lines and tall lowercase give the heading a loud, odd shape, and the body's modest thick-thin strokes settle everything beneath it.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-serif-lao: Cut-open terminals that let the counters flow outward make Gugi look ruled and compassed rather than handwritten. Noto Serif Lao follows with gentle weight shifts that shimmer faintly across a paragraph, giving a long read a bookish, authoritative hush.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-serif-makasar: Gugi's tall lowercase nearly touches its capitals, drawn in one uniform stroke. Noto Serif Makasar offsets that with thin strokes about half the weight of its thick ones, and that editorial give is what makes the pair work.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-serif-malayalam: Noto Serif Malayalam brings big open counters and bowls that thin gracefully where curves meet stems. And Gugi's strokes never swell or thin, so a long paragraph underneath feels like a soft, bookish exhale after a firm statement.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-serif-np-hmong: Gugi's flat fineliner line and cut-open terminals make each heading look bold and mechanically drawn, with tall lowercase. Noto Serif NP Hmong brings the stress in its o and e, a charcoal-soft touch.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-serif-old-uyghur: Gugi draws its letters as if with a round-tipped pen, bold and distinctive in tall lowercase forms. Noto Serif Old Uyghur takes the quieter job, with blown-glass bowls and mild thick-thin variation.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-serif-oriya: Dignified is the word for Noto Serif Oriya, whose curves run a little heavier than its joins, while Gugi draws everything with one fixed nib. Their strongest quality is that fixed-nib boldness against moderate contrast.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-serif-ottoman-siyaq: Noto Serif Ottoman Siyaq has bowls that swell only slightly and strokes narrowing gradually toward the terminals, a classic, dignified body. Gugi's wire-bent look is the louder partner, and that tension is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-serif-sinhala: Gugi draws a thread of ink, never swelling or tapering. Under it, Noto Serif Sinhala adds a lightly shaded texture and short stalks above a tall band of letters, so the bold heading and the bookish body each keep their own character.
gen-gf-gugi-gf-noto-serif-telugu: Noto Serif Telugu is gentle and traditional. Gugi's stencil-cut strokes of single weight feel flat and bold beside its softly shifting thick and thin, and the two sit together like a loud voice and a patient one.
